summary: Atari's Centipede is a trackball arcade fixed shooter with many home ports, compilations, and modern Recharged/anniversary routes.

entries.title: Centipede
entries.definitive_edition: Atari 50 arcade Centipede for current access; original cabinet for strict trackball fidelity

emulation.emulator: Atari 50 built-in emulation or MAME for cabinet comparison
emulation.notes: Original cabinet/trackball is the historical ceiling; Atari 50 is the practical official route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original arcade cabinet, or Atari 50 arcade version with input mapping documented

primary.version: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration, with arcade version selected
primary.why: Atari 50 is the best current official archive route because it includes Centipede inside a curated Atari history package, while the arcade original remains the trackball fidelity target. Centipede: Recharged is a modern reimagining and should be labeled separately.
primary.how_to_play: Use Atari 50 and select the arcade Centipede version, or use original arcade hardware/MAME for strict trackball fidelity. Record compilation version, arcade or home port selection, input device/trackball mapping, display/scaling, score, lives, and whether Recharged was excluded.

secondary.exclusive_content: Trackball cabinet control and CRT presentation
secondary.what_to_play: Use for strict historical control fidelity.
secondary.why: Modern compilations are accessible but may not match cabinet input feel.

secondary.exclusive_content: Modern reimagining with co-op and challenge modes
secondary.what_to_play: Use only as a remake/comparison route.
secondary.why: It is not the original 1981 arcade game.

all_releases.fidelity: Current official compilation route including arcade and home Atari versions.
all_releases.reason: primary: best current official access path.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Atari 50 is the best current route; cabinet input fidelity and Recharged remake behavior differ.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record port/version and input device, especially if using a stick instead of trackball.
